summary: This review (Le Merrer, Becker, Befort and Kieffer, Physiol Rev 2009) summarizes how the brain's endogenous opioid system controls hedonic responses and is altered by drugs of abuse in rodents. It covers the anatomy of opioid receptors and peptides, intracerebral pharmacology of reinforcement and feeding, gene knockout studies, and changes in opioid gene expression after chronic drug exposure. The excerpt provided focuses on the anatomy of the opioid system and on food reinforcement, especially opioid effects in the nucleus accumbens, ventral tegmental area, ventral pallidum, hypothalamus and amygdala.
one_line: Review of how the brain's opioid system mediates reward, hedonic responses and drug addiction in rodent models.
key_facts: The opioid system consists of three receptors: mu, delta, and kappa, activated by endogenous opioid peptides processed from proopiomelanocortin, proenkephalin, and prodynorphin.
Heroin was synthesized chemically by morphine diacetylation in the late 1800s and was commercialized as the first nonaddictive opiate to treat cough and asthma.
Both heroin and opium were prohibited in 1910.
The existence of opioid binding sites in the brain was established in 1973.
In 1975, Met- and Leu-enkephalin were characterized as the first endogenous ligands for opioid receptors.
The opioid receptor gene family includes four members: mu (Oprm1), delta (Oprd1), kappa (Oprk1), and the nonopioid orphaninFQ/nociceptin (Oprl1) receptors.
Mu is the most expressed opioid receptor in the amygdala (but not the central nucleus), thalamus, mesencephalon, and some brain stem nuclei.

Kappa binding sites only are found in seven brain regions that are part of the stress axis, including the claustrum, paraventricular hypothalamus, arcuate nucleus, supraoptic nucleus, median eminence, central amygdala, and pituitary.
Ligand autoradiography studies failed to detect significant kappa binding in the hippocampus, although pharmacological and electrophysiological data indicate kappa receptors are present there.
Penk is the most abundant and widely distributed opioid precursor and is best detected in the thalamus, where it overlaps with mu receptors.
POMC cell bodies are only detected in three regions: the arcuate nucleus of the hypothalamus, the nucleus tractus solitarius, and the pituitary.
Systemic mu and, to a lesser extent, delta agonists produce positive reinforcement, whereas kappa agonists induce aversion, hallucinations, and malaise.
Injections of mu or delta but not kappa receptor agonists into the NAc or VTA stimulate feeding.
Pecina and Berridge demonstrated that the shell of the nucleus accumbens contains a hedonic hotspot where mu receptor stimulation increases the 'liking' for food reward.
Compared with NAc and VTA receptors, pallidal mu opioid receptors are the most efficient in modulating food intake.

entities.name: Le Merrer, Becker, Befort and Kieffer
entities.role: authors of the review Reward Processing by the Opioid System in the Brain

entities.name: Physiol Rev
entities.role: journal in which the review was published (2009 Oct; 89(4): 1379–1412)

entities.name: Opium
entities.role: substance extracted from poppy seeds (Papaver somniferum) with pain-relieving and euphoric properties

entities.name: Morphine
entities.role: most active ingredient of opium and the most widely used pain killer in contemporary medicine

entities.name: Heroin
entities.role: chemically synthesized from morphine by diacetylation; a main illicit drug of abuse

entities.name: Met- and Leu-enkephalin
entities.role: two pentapeptides characterized in 1975 as the first endogenous ligands for opioid receptors

entities.name: Nucleus accumbens (NAc)
entities.role: brain region where mu receptor agonists stimulate feeding and which contains a hedonic hotspot in its shell

entities.name: Ventral tegmental area (VTA)
entities.role: origin of mesolimbic dopaminergic projections; site where opioid agonists stimulate feeding

entities.name: Ventral pallidum (VP)
entities.role: major output structure of the NAc with a hedonic hotspot in its posterior section

entities.name: Central nucleus of the amygdala (CeA)
entities.role: amygdala region where DAMGO increased food intake and naltrexone decreased intake of preferred diets

entities.name: Paraventricular hypothalamus (PVN)
entities.role: hypothalamic nucleus where mu receptor activation increases food intake

entities.name: Lateral hypothalamus (LH)
entities.role: hypothalamic site where morphine injection stimulated feeding

entities.name: Arcuate nucleus (Arc)
entities.role: hypothalamic nucleus that is one of three regions with POMC cell bodies

entities.name: Nucleus tractus solitarius (NTS)
entities.role: brain stem region with POMC cell bodies

entities.name: DAMGO
entities.role: mu receptor agonist injected intracerebrally to increase feeding and flavor consumption

entities.name: Naltrexone
entities.role: opioid receptor antagonist that decreased consumption of preferred food and blocked DAMGO-induced feeding

entities.name: Pecina and Berridge
entities.role: researchers who identified the hedonic hotspot in the nucleus accumbens shell
